title: basic-auth user password change: SqlAlchemyStore.update_user enforces the 12-character minimum (_validate_password) before hashing, same as create_user
answers: Why can an admin reset a basic-auth user's password to a short value through the update-user-password API?
Where is the minimum password length for basic-auth users checked when a password is changed?
What error comes back when a password update is shorter than the policy allows, and is the old password kept?
Does an update that only changes is_admin still work when no password is sent?
body:
Path: Basic-auth user management that sets or changes a local user's password (create-user, update-user-password, admin resets, signup and bootstrap flows that go through the store) runs through mlflow/server/auth/sqlalchemy_store.py:update_user and create_user. The password-strength check is mlflow/utils/validation.py:_validate_password.
Rule: update_user calls _validate_password(password) inside its `if password is not None:` branch, before generate_password_hash, so the same minimum that create_user enforces applies to every password change. Validation sits before the hash assignment, so a rejected update leaves the stored password_hash unchanged. Keep the check before hashing if this block changes.
Symptom: A user or admin could set a password shorter than the 12-character policy through update_user / update_user_password, even though creating a user with the same password was rejected.
Constraints: Applies only when a password is supplied; is_admin-only updates (password None) skip the check and behave as before. The error is INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE with the message "Password must be at least 12 characters." (the message in validation.py now matches the len(password) < 12 guard). Tests that exercise successful creates or updates should use passwords well above 12 characters (the new test uses random_str(size=20)), and a changed password should be asserted by checking the old one no longer authenticates.
Applies: Any code path in the basic-auth store that creates or changes a local user's password; does not cover password checks in other auth providers.
applies: Basic-auth local user password creation and updates in the tracking auth store; not for is_admin-only changes or non-basic-auth providers.
says: Admins can reset an account password to a value shorter than the required minimum.
Users can update their password to fewer than twelve characters, bypassing security policy.
Password changes should enforce the exact same length requirements as new account creation.
When a password update is rejected for length, the existing password must remain active.
Updating user administrator status without providing a new password should continue to succeed.
search: SqlAlchemyStore.update_user in mlflow/server/auth/sqlalchemy_store.py calls _validate_password before generate_password_hash when password is not None, enforcing the 12-character minimum on password changes identical to create_user. Placing validation before hashing ensures that a rejected update raises INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE with 'Password must be at least 12 characters.' while leaving the stored password hash unchanged. Updates modifying only is_admin pass password as None and bypass validation without error. Applies to local basic-auth user creation and password update operations in the tracking auth store, excluding non-basic-auth providers.
